<!-- Generated by ModuleDocsGenerator from the documentation of org.hortonmachine.modules.LinesPolygonizer: do not edit, change the annotations and regenerate. -->

In the **faces** mode the lines are first noded, cut where they cross, so lines that cross without sharing a vertex still close a face. Every face the network encloses becomes a polygon, also the ones between other faces: a line that closes onto itself makes a polygon, a line that ends in nothing (a dangle) or only connects two faces (a cut edge) does not. The number of the lines that were not used is reported in the log.

In the **join** mode the lines of each group, all the lines when no group field is given, are chained into one ring: from the end of a line the chain goes on with the line that has the nearest end, reversing it if needed, and the last line is joined to the first. Gaps between the lines are closed with a straight segment, which suits outlines digitized in pieces. The groups whose ring crosses itself are reported and left out.

The id of a polygon is taken from the point of the points layer that lies in it, if a points layer is given, else from the group in the join mode, else it is a progressive number from 1. Polygons with no point get no id.
